text:
anya: Heads-up — ran into a subtle auth/config combo when trying to run redwoodctl inside our VS Code devcontainer. install succeeded but local-serve couldn't find the token and spawned login which blocked the container start.

derek: hmm. devcontainer envs often change HOME. Did the install write to /root vs /workspace?

anya: yes. Installer (tarball) defaulted to /usr/local/bin, but my devcontainer sets HOME=/workspace. redwoodctl wrote profiles to /root/.redwood. local-serve looks for $PWD/.redwood first, then $HOME/.redwood. mismatch.

frank: Oof. That's easy to miss. We should prioritize REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR env var if set, and otherwise print where we looked when no token found. Right now it just says "no token".

anya: Exactly. The error we saw was literally one line: "auth failed" and a spinner. Spent 20 mins checking GH secrets.

ci-bot: Reminder: CI/devcontainers should set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR to a shared path to avoid per-user confusion. See https://internal.example.com/dev/devcontainers#redwoodctl

derek: Workarounds that worked for me in devcontainer:
1) set environment in .devcontainer.json:
   "containerEnv": { "REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR": "/workspace/.redwood" }
2) create a shim so spawned processes see same config: ~/bin/redwoodctl -> exec /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl --config-dir /workspace/.redwood

anya: I did that, but also hit a second problem: the shim was in /home/vscode/bin but PATH for the systemd user in the container didn't include it, so the spawned login still used /usr/local/bin and ignored our --config-dir.

frank: ugh. spawn environments are tricky. local-serve should explicitly pass the config-dir flag when calling subprocesses instead of relying on PATH shims. Also detect non-tty and prefer device flow with printed URL.

anya: Another wrinkle: our devcontainer uses a bind-mounted workspace from mac host and the host's permissions are 501:20. redwoodctl attempted to create a profiles.lock using flock and failed with EOPNOTSUPP over the mount. error: "lock failed: operation not supported".

frank: NFS/fuse/host mounts can break file locking. We should switch to an advisory fallback: if file lock fails, use a local ephemeral lock in /tmp keyed by project + hostname. Non-ideal but avoids hard crash for dev.

ci-bot: Note: Locking issues on mounted volumes are a known class. See infra note: LOCK-44 for advisory fallback options.

derek: For CI we solved it by setting REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR to an emptyDir (tmp) and copying profiles.json in during setup. Example step in GitHub Actions:

```
- name: Prepare redwood config
  run: |
    mkdir -p /tmp/redwood-config
    echo "$REDWOOD_PROFILES_JSON" > /tmp/redwood-config/profiles.json
  env:
    REDWOOD_PROFILES_JSON: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_PROFILES_JSON }}
- name: Run local serve
  run: redwoodctl local-serve --config-dir /tmp/redwood-config
```

This bypasses mount lock problems.

anya: Good tip. I also added REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1 to the Dockerfile during `npm ci -g redwoodctl` to avoid postinstall login that expects a tty. That prevented the installer step from stalling in builds.

frank: Nice. Two UX suggestions from this thread:
1) local-serve should accept `--config-dir` and always pass it to spawned redwoodctl commands.
2) When auth spawn falls back to device flow, print the device URL and code to the parent logs immediately and include a one-line hint: "If running in container/devcontainer, set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR and use --no-open".

ci-bot: Feature request created: PDE-801 local-serve should propagate config-dir/env to child processes and improve spawned-auth logging.

anya: Also propose a small CLI change: `redwoodctl login --device --no-open` should exit with a distinct exit code (e.g., 11) when it printed a device URL, so orchestrators can detect a non-fatal interactive-required state. Right now it's exit 1 and CI misinterprets it as failure.

frank: Agree. Exit-code taxonomy is useful: 10=auth failure, 11=device-flow-pending (printed URL), 12=network error. Makes automation simpler.

derek: Quick doc PR I'll open: add a "Devcontainer and mounts" troubleshooting section with the shim/snippet and GH Actions example. I'll also add the `--config-dir` recommendation to the sample-app quickstart.

anya: Thanks. I pushed a small GH gist with the devcontainer snippet: https://gist.github.com/anya/devcontainer-redwood-config (draft). I'll convert to a PR after phone call.

devex-bot: PR created: docs/devcontainer-config-dir-guidance (refs PDE-801). Assigned to @devex.

anya: One last tiny note — when redwoodctl detects multiple profile stores (e.g., /workspace/.redwood and /root/.redwood), print a clear warning listing both and which one will be used. That would have saved my time.

frank: agreed. We'll add a warning on startup and a `redwoodctl config sources` command to list possible stores and precedence.

anya: Great. Thanks everyone — feel free to ping me if you want me to validate the PR in a devcontainer. Closing after docs + CLI changes land. :sparkles:
